articles.title: Hiding inside Palantir's skyrocketing quarter is a foreboding signal | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Palantir's U.S. commercial revenue surpassed U.S. government revenue for the first time ever.
articles.body_text: The data analysis company Palantir delivered such a huge third-quarter earnings report on Monday that its press release even bragged that the numbers were “crushing consensus expectations.” Yet retail investors were lukewarm on the company on Tuesday, with the stock trading slightly down. That’s because Palantir’s enterprise sales, its big growth area, showed signs of slowing. First, the good news for the company’s investors. Revenue grew 96% from a year earlier, and 20% from the previous quarter, to $2.31 billion, beating analysts’ expectations of $2.18 billion. It was the first time Palantir has topped $2 billion in a quarter. Palantir also reported adjusted earnings per share (profit per share, excluding certain one-time items) of 44 cents, compared with analysts’ expectations of 41 cents. The company even raised its revenue guidance, or forecast, for the full year. Normally, that alone would send a stock soaring. The clincher was that Palantir’s U.S. commercial revenue surpassed U.S. government revenue for the first time ever. The company reported $984 million in commercial contracts (up 148% from the year-ago quarter), versus $953 million in U.S. government revenue. The reason for all this love from enterprises? They are signing up for the company’s AI software that can run frontier models and custom-train open-weight models securely, without sharing any of their data and business processes with outside AI labs. Plus, Palantir has long offered what is today known as “forward-deployed” software engineering, in which its own engineers work directly with customers to customize the software. However, Palantir also revealed a less-than-rosy signal: Even as enterprises are moving faster than ever, they are often signing short-term trials. “What Ryan and I are seeing on the front line and commercial is this much quicker interaction, much quicker to deployment, shorter duration of the contract but then an ability to expand that contract dramatically,” CEO Alex Karp (pictured above) told Wall Street analysts on the quarterly earnings call. Palantir is experiencing one of the unique phenomena of AI in the enterprise right now. Corporations are willing to quickly try AI software, skipping the usual bureaucracy, but they are also more willing to cancel contracts. Karp used one off-color metaphor after another to describe how unconcerned he was about holding onto his enterprise business. “We’ve gone from being the most attractive person in the physics department to being the captain of the football team, kind of thing,” he said, describing the influx of prospective corporate customers flowing in. “Conversely, you know, once you go Palantir, you don’t go back, and that’s just how it is, and you see it in our numbers.” The numbers don’t yet confirm Palantir’s long-term success. While the company closed a hefty $1.46 billion of total contract value from U.S. enterprises in the quarter, that’s actually a decline from the record $2.13 billion in the previous quarter. That suggests slowing sales, at least in the most recent quarter. The next earnings will show whether Palantir has solidified its role as a rising U.S. enterprise AI provider. Historically, many enterprises sign their biggest tech purchases in the final quarter of the year. Karp and his team certainly sound confident. They increased guidance for U.S. commercial revenue to be “in excess of $3.559 billion, representing a growth rate of at least 143%.”

articles.title: Anthropic is still grappling with the economics of compute | TechCrunch
articles.summary: At a moment when Anthropic's compute margins should be getting better, they’re getting worse.
articles.body_text: There’s a lot of mystery around the finances of major AI labs, and as Anthropic inches towards it IPO, we’re starting to get some answers. In particular, the company is finally disclosing more about the economics of compute, and how much of Anthropic’s skyrocketing revenue is being lost to compute costs. In a new filing on Monday , Anthropic released data that showed those margins on compute actually getting worse. The filing was an update to the S-1 released last week — but where that filing’s financial disclosures only covered through June 30 of this year, the new data extended to disclose results through an extra quarter, to September 30. Broadly, Anthropic had a good quarter: revenue reached $17 billion, up from $11.5 billion in the previous quarter, suggesting durable growth. But the operating loss grew at the same time, thanks in large part to growing compute costs. Looking at the compute margins makes the picture even worse. In the new quarter, compute took up 58% of the company’s revenue, up from 48% the quarter before. At a moment when the company could win over IPO investors by showing margins improving, they’re getting worse. A chart in the filing shows this even more clearly, tracking the company’s revenue for every dollar spent on compute. Since the start of 2025, it’s been steadily growing, peaking at just over 2x this past quarter, then falling back down to 1.72x. Many indications imply that this shift in compute margins is more of a blip than a long-term problem, but it still tells us important things about the business of running a major lab. Trying to keep up with demand, Anthropic’s compute bill shot up to $10 billion for the quarter, including, as the filing notes, “$5.0 billion of compute under short-term commitments, which currently costs significantly more than comparable compute procured under our multi-year commitments.” Basically, demand was growing so fast that Anthropic had to scramble for compute, which meant paying higher rates. Some of those deals have already played out in public. Anthropic has been paying SpaceX $1.25 billion a month for compute, alongside multibillion-dollar deals with Nscale , Akamai , and Volta . In the parlance of the industry, these are neoclouds rather than hyperscalers — smaller outfits that offer more flexible compute deals at higher rates. Anthropic’s margins got worse in Q3 because of deals like these, and there’s no sign they’ll be able to do without them anytime soon. As the new filing puts it, “We expect compute and infrastructure expenses to increase in absolute dollars and remain our largest operating expense for the foreseeable future as additional committed compute becomes available to us under multi-year arrangements with CSPs, and as we continue to invest in additional compute.” Anthropic is still trying to lower its compute costs. In particular, the company talks quite a bit about its efforts to build its own compute base under a project it calls “Anthropic Direct.” But with demand growing so fast, those efforts aren’t going to be able to keep pace, and the neoclouds will continue to be the best option they have. In a sense, these are champagne problems. As long as revenue is growing at nearly 50% a quarter, few investors will worry about high compute costs — and the moment demand slows down, investors may be comforted by a compute picture that has gotten a lot sunnier. But it’s a reminder of how much AI labs still depend on the trillion-dollar infrastructure buildout — and how vulnerable they are to hiccups in that process. It’s easy to imagine the data center buildout slowing down over the next year if bond markets get skittish or local opposition gets more intense. There’s not much Anthropic can do to address either of those risks, and either one would make a messy compute picture a whole lot messier. In the meantime, the future of Anthropic and other labs will be at the mercy of compute prices. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.body_text: Republikanernas nederlag i mellanårsvalet beror på kriget i Iran. Det hävdar vicepresident JD Vance, som nu bryter tystnaden efter valförlusten. ”Presidenten själv sa det i går kväll”, skriver han i ett inlägg på X . Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Men SEB:s USA-ekonom Elisabet Kopelman tonar ned farhågorna. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. En blå våg sveper över USA . Efter nattens mellanårsval ser Demokraterna ut att ta kontroll över både representanthuset och senaten. Valresultatet har skapat oro på den amerikanska teknikmarknaden, där flera AI-relaterade aktier föll i förhandeln. Investerare befarar att det ska bromsa utbyggnaden av datacenter, som är avgörande för den snabbt växande sektorn. En av dem som varnar för konsekvenserna är teknikanalytikern Dan Ives. Han beskriver Demokraternas framgång som ett ”seismiskt skifte” för AI-industrin som kan få återverkningar under flera år. Enligt Ives riskerar Republikanernas förlust att bromsa utbyggnaden av de 800–1 000 datacenter som planeras runtom i USA. – Svaret är enligt vår uppfattning ett klart ja, säger han om risken för en inbromsning, enligt The Telegraph. Men SEB:s USA-ekonom Elisabet Kopelman gör en annan bedömning. – Jag tror inte att ett demokratiskt styre i kongressen kommer att ha så stor påverkan, säger hon till Expressen. Hon pekar bland annat på rädslan för att hamna på efterkälken i förhållande till Kina, men också på att teknikaktierna varit en viktig drivkraft bakom börsuppgångarna.

Oktobers attacker mot franska matbutiker har skapat oro även hos svenska matbutiker. Samma natt som de franska blodkylarna angreps slogs även kylar ut i flera svenska Ica och Coop-butiker. Även Axfoods lager drabbades, något som Expressen tidigare har rapporterat om . Jon Ossoff, sittande senator i Georgia, vann en enkel seger i delstatens senatsval i år. Bara några minuter efter att vallokalerna i Georgia hade stängt utropades han till segrare och med nästan alla röster räknade står det klart att han får 59 procent av Georgiabornas röster. Nu tror vissa att han om två år ska kunna utmana om segern i ett annat val – presidentvalet. Vadslagningssajten Polymarket håller just nu Jon Ossoff som klar favorit till att bli Demokraternas presidentkandidat 2028. Under natten klättrade han med 9 procentenheter till 24 procents sannolikhet att få nomineringen, enligt de som vadslår på sajten. Det innebär att han ligger före bland annat kongressledamoten Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez och Kaliforniens guvernör Gavin Newsom. Samma mönster syns på sajten Kalshi, en annan vadslagsningssajt. 39-åringen är USA :s yngste senator och har på senare tid fått många blickar riktade mot sig, då han anses ha en förmåga att samla stöd från Demokraternas många olika falanger. Han har bland annat liknats vid Barack Obama, och har under valrörelsens gång även fått stort stöd från den tidigare presidenten. Jon Ossoff har dock sagt att han inte är intresserad av att ställa upp som president, då han vill fokusera på jobbet som senator och på sin familj. articles.body_text: Jokkmokks kommunchef Lars Eriksson har producerat och medverkat i porrfilmer som släpptes 2025 och 2026, avslöjar SVT Nyheter Norrbotten. Den 19 oktober arbetsbefriades Eriksson. En vecka senare fick han tillbaka tjänsten, men utan ansvar för personal, ekonomi och budget. Kommunen kände då inte till uppgifterna om porrfilmerna, enligt SVT.
